summary: Transient shaper for drums, buses and masters: Attack and Sustain gains (±12 dB) on the onset and the body of what comes in, found by two followers of its level (Punchy, Balanced or Smooth), with an optional lookahead so the gain is already there at the first sample. Impact mode splits into four bands (zero-latency Linkwitz–Riley crossovers) and moves each band's microdynamics (its short-term level against its long-term level) with one bipolar knob, with auto gain per band. Left/right or mid/side, Mix, Delta (hear only what it changes) and a gain-match reading. Use it on a drum bus for snap or tail control, and on a master in small moves.
use_for: Add or remove attack and sustain on drums, buses and masters.

parameters.name: Attack
parameters.description: Gain on the onsets (the first milliseconds of a hit), 0.1 dB steps. 0 dB with Sustain at 0 dB passes the audio bit for bit
parameters.how: Adds or removes up to 12 dB of gain on the onsets, the first milliseconds of a hit.
parameters.sound: Positive values make hits punchier and sharper; negative values soften them.

parameters.name: Sustain
parameters.description: Gain on the body and the tail after the onset, 0.1 dB steps
parameters.how: Adds or removes up to 12 dB of gain on the body and tail after the onset.
parameters.sound: Positive values make notes longer and fuller; negative values dry the sound out.

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: The followers' time constants. Punchy: onsets of 0.1 ms, fast release. Balanced: the default. Smooth: slower, for bass and long hits
parameters.how: Chooses how quickly the followers react: Punchy, Balanced or Smooth.
parameters.sound: Punchy suits short hits, Smooth suits bass and long sounds.

parameters.name: Lookahead
parameters.description: The audio is delayed this long so the gain is already up at the first sample of a hit (reported to NeoBuzz Live and compensated; 0 is no latency, and the first millisecond of a hit then gets less of the Attack gain)
parameters.how: Delays the audio by up to 5 ms so the gain is ready on the first sample of a hit.
parameters.sound: Attack changes act on the very start of a hit, at the cost of a little latency.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Attack/Sustain: the two gains above. Impact: four bands, each with its microdynamics moved by its Impact knob (Attack and Sustain are not used)
parameters.how: Chooses Attack/Sustain gains, or Impact, which has a separate microdynamics control for each of four bands.
parameters.sound: Impact lets you sharpen the highs while smoothing the lows, or the reverse.

parameters.name: Crossover 1
parameters.description: Between the first and the second band (Impact mode)
parameters.how: Sets the frequency between the first and second band in Impact mode, from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
parameters.sound: It decides how much of the low end is treated as the lowest band.

parameters.name: Crossover 2
parameters.description: Between the second and the third band (never below Crossover 1)
parameters.how: Sets the frequency between the second and third band in Impact mode.
parameters.sound: It moves the boundary between the lower and upper midrange.

parameters.name: Crossover 3
parameters.description: Between the third and the fourth band (never below Crossover 2)
parameters.how: Sets the frequency between the third and fourth band in Impact mode.
parameters.sound: It decides where the top band begins.

parameters.name: Impact 1
parameters.description: The first band's microdynamics: −100 % takes them out (the band follows its slow level), +100 % doubles them (in dB), 0 leaves them
parameters.how: Sets the first band's microdynamics from -100 % (flattened) to +100 % (doubled).
parameters.sound: Positive values make low hits livelier; negative values smooth the bass out.

parameters.name: Impact 2
parameters.how: Sets the second band's microdynamics from -100 % to +100 %.
parameters.sound: Positive values add punch to the lower midrange, negative values soften it.

parameters.name: Impact 3
parameters.how: Sets the third band's microdynamics from -100 % to +100 %.
parameters.sound: Positive values add snap to snares and vocals, negative values soften them.

parameters.name: Impact 4
parameters.how: Sets the fourth band's microdynamics from -100 % to +100 %.
parameters.sound: Positive values add crispness to cymbals and hats, negative values soften them.

parameters.name: Auto gain
parameters.description: Impact mode: each band's energy stays what it was whatever its Impact (a 300 ms average, within ±12 dB)
parameters.how: Keeps each band's loudness the same whatever its Impact, in Impact mode.
parameters.sound: You hear the change in feel rather than a change in volume.

parameters.name: Stereo
parameters.description: What is shaped: left and right (one gain for both, from the louder), or mid and side (each its own)
parameters.how: Chooses whether the shaping works on left and right, or on mid and side.
parameters.sound: Mid/side lets the centre and the width be shaped separately; left/right keeps one gain for both sides.

parameters.name: Mix
parameters.description: Dry/wet (the dry signal is delayed to match)
parameters.how: Blends the shaped signal with the dry signal.
parameters.sound: Lower values give a subtler effect that keeps more of the original dynamics.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Gain after the shaper, 0.1 dB steps (the editor's Match sets it from the gain-match reading)
parameters.how: Adds -24 to +24 dB of gain after the shaper.
parameters.sound: It matches the loudness to the untreated sound so you judge the punch fairly.

parameters.name: Delta
parameters.description: Hear only what the shaper changes: the output minus the input, delayed to match (gliding over 10 ms)
parameters.how: Plays only the difference between the output and the input.
parameters.sound: You hear only what the shaper adds or removes, which shows how much the hits have changed.

readings.description: Short-term loudness out − in (K-weighted, 3 s): what Output would have to take back for equal loudness
The largest gain applied (to one band, in Impact mode)
The smallest gain applied (negative: the most it took away)
How much of the time the audio was in an onset (Attack/Sustain mode)
The lookahead, reported to NeoBuzz Live
